data.name: New MaxxBench Reveals AI Coding Models' Fragility to Tiny Changes
data.summary: MaxxBench perturbs 89 DeepSWE tasks with minor changes like altered timestamps, causing models that hit 74% on originals to spread out by 23 points. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash drops from 74.2% to 55.6%, while Claude Opus 5.5 rises slightly to 76.4%—the only one to improve. Despite its popularity for speed, low cost, and strong real-world results like spotting cybersecurity issues for $12, the benchmark highlights over-optimization for specific tests. Platforms like Vercel and Perch are expanding free access to fast variants, sharpening focus on practical reliability.

GPT-6.1-sol leads the leaderboard at 66.02, excelling in objects and scenes, while strengths shine in local mechanics at 83.08 but drop sharply in movement and stateful workflows. The open benchmark reveals cost tradeoffs and guides developers on picking agents for specific 3D needs, highlighting the gap between demos and full games.
data.hook: Coding agents that ace software tasks now face real 3D challenges, from crafting objects to building interactive worlds in Blender and Unreal Engine.

data.name: TermiX Agent Marketplace Hits $30 Million in Transactions
data.summary: TermiX reported over $30.45 million in transaction volume on its Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol, with 1.31 million agents indexed across BNB Chain and Base, plus 588,000 cumulative jobs and $609K in protocol revenue. In one example, the Montage Studio agent coordinates others to turn a short promo brief into a finished 1080p video, managing payments through on-chain escrow. While some observers see this as proof the agent economy is maturing, analysts call for more transparent job receipts to verify the numbers fully.

data.name: SenseTime Unveils SenseNova 6.8 with Persistent Memory and Editable Outputs
data.summary: SenseNova 6.8 Flash stands out for its long-term memory, carrying goals and constraints through conversations while generating editable assets like animated PPTs, motion posters, interactive websites, and Blender 3D projects. Users highlight how it shifts from repeated briefings to seamless, proactive assistance in office tasks and design. Alongside, the open-source SenseNova 6.8 Code2Video lets creators build videos via modifiable code, available on GitHub and Hugging Face, with the full model free via Raccoon assistant until December 1. Benchmarks show it competing strongly in memory and agent tasks, pointing to a future of iterative, context-aware AI tools.

data.name: Atmanity Launches Atmee v2 for Lifelike AI Video Avatars
data.summary: Chen-Ping Yu, who once sold his AR startup to Google, unveiled Atmee v2 this week as the next big interface after text and voice. From one image and 10 seconds of audio, it generates expressive avatars that handle live conversations, full-body movements, and environmental interactions—running 50 times faster and far cheaper than rivals like Seedance 2.5. Developers can use its API for tutors, game NPCs, or companions, with demos showing fictional characters like 'Jean Philanthrope' holding natural talks. Early feedback praises immersive potential but raises worries about scams and over-reliance on human-like AI.

data.name: Cluely CEO Reveals Thesis Behind Viral Apps and Content Strategy
data.summary: Cluely's CEO Roy Lee clarified the startup isn't just an app studio, despite launching consumer apps like Dare for AI editing, Line for language learning, and ReGen for dating photos under Bounty Studio. These tested a thesis on using viral reels, paid creators, and shareable formats to drive success, now validated and seen as a path to major profits. The strategy builds on Cluely's roots as an AI desktop assistant for real-time suggestions, fueled by bold moves like their 'cheat on everything' launch after a university suspension that drew $15 million from Andreessen Horowitz. Observers note distribution trumps building in AI, with office prank videos channeling attention into a self-reinforcing loop.

data.name: AI Videos Trap Supermarket Worker in Endless Clone Maze
data.summary: Using Flova 1.5, people generate chilling videos of a supermarket employee lost in warping, infinite aisles where identical versions of himself multiply around every corner. The story unfolds from a normal store entrance to unease at checkout, then pure disorientation with clones in formation. Flova's Liminal Space Horror skill warps the layout for dread, while Multi-View Character ensures every clone looks identical across shots, creating low-budget horror with a modern twist that feels genuinely unsettling.

data.name: World Labs Launches Frameboy: Playable Real-Time World Model
data.summary: Frameboy is a browser-based demo from World Labs that lets users control a camera inside Atlas-generated scenes, streaming up to 15 frames per second with keyboard or mouse input. It features a fun Game Boy-style interface where you pick scenes like atriums or plazas, then move around as the model generates views frame by frame in about 70 milliseconds. Built on an optimized Atlas from two months ago, it integrates with the Viewfinder app for custom scenes and heads toward interactive experiences like cloud gaming. You can jump in at frameboy.worldlabs.ai.
data.hook: Fei-Fei Li invited everyone to try real-time Atlas with a simple message: 'Real time Atlas! Try it now!' Now, anyone can grab a virtual camera and explore generated worlds right in their browser.

data.name: Seedance 2.5 Lets AI Transform Sets Around Real Actors
data.summary: Seedance 2.5, a ByteDance video model on platforms like Higgsfield, excels at video-to-video changes that preserve camera moves, faces, dialogue, and timing from real footage. It swaps in new locations, lighting, and effects, like placing performers in burning ruins or adding intricate face details without makeup. Creators highlight examples with Nicolas Cage in dramatic scenes and note it handles 30-second clips with synced audio, making cinematic visuals more accessible without high production costs.
